```{r, setup, include=FALSE}
# >>> LOAD LIBRARIES <<< #
library(flexdashboard)
library(plotly)
library(dplyr)
library(DT)
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)
library(data.table)
library(htmltools)
```

```{r, global, include=FALSE, echo=FALSE, error=TRUE}
# Create global variables and functions
# Set Table number to account for optional tables
table_number <- 0

# Read QC csv file
summary_df <- read.table(params$summary_df, header = TRUE, sep = ",")

# Specify and create a df with negative controls
control_substrings = trimws(strsplit(params$neg_ctrl_substrings, "[,;|]+")[[1]])
control_regex = paste(control_substrings, collapse = "|")
is_control <- grepl(
  control_regex,
  summary_df$sample,
  ignore.case = TRUE
)
has_controls <- any(is_control)
control_df <- summary_df[is_control, ]

# Genome completeness colour palette
get_genome_completeness_color <- function(value) {
  # Create the Red to Yellow to Green color palette for 100 values
  red_to_green_palette <- colorRampPalette(c("#FF0039", "#FF7518", "#3FB618"))(100)

  # Calculate the index of the color in the palette based on the input value
  if (value == 0) {
    value <- value + 0.00001
  }
  color_index <- ceiling(value * 100)

  # Return the corresponding color with alpha 0.7
  selected_color <- red_to_green_palette[color_index]
  selected_color <- adjustcolor(selected_color, alpha = 0.7)
  return(selected_color)
}

# Horizontal Line function for plotly
hline <- function(y = 0, color = "black") {
  list(
    type = "line",
    x0 = 0,
    x1 = 1,
    xref = "paper",
    y0 = y,
    y1 = y,
    line = list(color = color, dash = "dash")
  )
}

# Create a new column based on the qc_pass value for colours
add_pass_value_int <- function(df, column) {
  # Split the column values on semicolons
  split_values <- strsplit(df[[column]], ';')

  # Define which int values go with which statement
  key_phrases <- c('PASS', 'PARTIAL_GENOME', 'INCOMPLETE_GENOME')
  values <- c(1, 2, 3)

  # Initialize a vector to store the results
  results <- integer(length(df[[column]]))

  for (i in 1:length(split_values)) {
    # Check if any key phrase is contained in the split values
    matching_phrases <- intersect(split_values[[i]], key_phrases)

    if (length(matching_phrases) > 0) {
      # If matching phrases are found, assign the corresponding integer value
      #  Technically none of the 3 key phrases can be output together but just in case go with highest value
      results[i] <- max(values[match(matching_phrases, key_phrases)])
    } else {
      results[i] <- 0  # If none of the key phrases are found, assign 0
    }
  }

  # Return results
  return(results)
}

# Function: Section Headers
catHeader <- function(text = "", level = 3) {
  cat(
    paste0(
      "\n\n",
      paste(rep("#", level), collapse = ""),
      " ",
      text,
      "\n\n"
    )
  )
}
```

Run Summary
==============================

Row
------------------------------

### Total Samples
```{r, samples_box, echo=FALSE, error=TRUE}
total_samples <- length(unique(summary_df[["sample"]]))
valueBox(total_samples, icon = "")
```

### Total Passing Samples
```{r, passing_box, echo=FALSE, error=TRUE}
if (isTRUE(params$segmented) && "reference" %in% colnames(summary_df)) {
  # A segmented sample is only fully passing if all of its segments pass
  sample_pass_status <- summary_df %>%
    group_by(sample) %>%
    summarise(fully_pass = all(qc_pass == "PASS"), .groups = "drop")
  passing_samples <- sum(sample_pass_status$fully_pass, na.rm = FALSE)
} else {
  passing_samples <- sum(summary_df[["qc_pass"]] == "PASS", na.rm = FALSE)
}
valueBox(passing_samples, icon = "")
```

```{r, results='asis', echo=FALSE, eval=isTRUE(params$segmented) && "reference" %in% colnames(summary_df)}
catHeader("Number of Segments", level = 3)
num_segments <- length(unique(as.character(summary_df$reference)))
valueBox(num_segments, icon = "")
```

### Run Name
```{r, run_name_box, echo=FALSE, error=TRUE}
if ("run_name" %in% colnames(summary_df)) {
  run_name <- summary_df[1, 'run_name']
} else {
  run_name <- "NA"
}
valueBox(run_name, icon = "")
```

### Negative Control Status
```{r, controls_status_box, echo=FALSE, error=TRUE}
# Based on run status, set colour and icon
run_status = summary_df[1, 'run_status']
if ( run_status == 'PASS' ) {
    sec_icon = ""
    sec_color = "success"
} else if ( run_status == 'WARN' ) {
    sec_icon = ""
    sec_color = "warning"
} else if ( run_status == 'NO_CONTROLS' ) {
    run_status = "NO CONTROLS"
    sec_icon = ""
    sec_color = "warning"
} else {
    sec_icon = ""
    sec_color = "danger"
}
valueBox(
  run_status,
  icon = sec_icon,
  color = sec_color
)
```

### {-}
```{r, plot_completeness, echo=FALSE, error=TRUE}
# Create a genome completeness plot, optionally selecting a segment.
df <- select(summary_df, sample, any_of("reference"), genome_completeness)

if (isTRUE(params$segmented) && "reference" %in% colnames(df)) {
  segment_data <- split(df, df$reference)
  segment_names <- names(segment_data)
  p <- plot_ly()

  # Custom red-yellow-green colorscale (green = high completeness, red = low)
  completeness_colorscale <- list(
    list(0, "rgb(165,0,38)"),
    list(0.5, "rgb(255,255,191)"),
    list(1, "rgb(0,104,55)")
  )

  for (i in seq_along(segment_data)) {
    p <- p %>%
      add_bars(
        data = segment_data[[i]],
        x = ~sample,
        y = ~genome_completeness,
        marker = list(
          color = ~genome_completeness,
          colorscale = completeness_colorscale,
          cmin = 0,
          cmax = 1,
          showscale = TRUE,
          colorbar = list(tickformat = ".0%", title = "")
        ),
        name = segment_names[[i]],
        visible = i == 1
      )
  }

  segment_buttons <- lapply(seq_along(segment_names), function(i) {
    visible <- rep(FALSE, length(segment_names))
    visible[[i]] <- TRUE

    list(
      label = segment_names[[i]],
      method = "update",
      args = list(
        list(visible = visible),
        list(title = segment_names[[i]])
      )
    )
  })

  p <- p %>%
    layout(
      title = segment_names[[1]],
      xaxis = list(title = "Sample Name"),
      yaxis = list(title = "Genome Completeness", tickformat = '.2%'),
      shapes = list(hline(0.9), hline(0.5)),
      updatemenus = list(list(
        type = "dropdown",
        direction = "down",
        x = 0,
        xanchor = "left",
        y = 1.12,
        yanchor = "top",
        pad = list(r = 0, t = 0),
        buttons = segment_buttons
      )),
      showlegend = FALSE
    )
} else {
  p <- plot_ly(
    df,
    x = ~sample,
    y = ~genome_completeness,
    type = 'bar',
    color = ~genome_completeness,
    colors = "RdYlGn",
    name = ""
  ) %>%
    layout(
      title = "Sample Genome Completeness",
      xaxis = list(title = "Sample Name"),
      yaxis = list(title = "Genome Completeness", tickformat = '.2%'),
      shapes = list(hline(0.9), hline(0.5))
    )
}

p
```

> **Figure 1.** Per Sample Genome Completeness. Comparison of the percentage of bases called in the consensus sequence of each sample.
> The dashed lines at 50% and 90% show the cut-offs for an incomplete genome and a partial genome respectively.

### {-}
```{r, data_table, echo=FALSE, error=TRUE}
# Create an interactive table of all samples with the different qc statuses highlighted
df <- summary_df %>%
  select(any_of(c('sample', 'reference', 'qc_pass', 'lineage', 'mean_sequencing_depth', 'median_sequencing_depth',
                  'num_aligned_reads', 'total_variants', 'num_snps', 'num_iupacs',
                  'num_deletions', 'num_deletion_sites', 'num_insertions',
                  'num_insertion_sites', 'genome_completeness')))

# Rename column names
df <- df %>%
  rename(
    "Sample" = sample,
    "Mean Depth" = mean_sequencing_depth,
    "Median Depth" = median_sequencing_depth,
    "Total Aligned Reads" = num_aligned_reads,
    "Variant Count" = total_variants,
    "# SNPs" = num_snps,
    "# Del" = num_deletions,
    "# Del Sites" = num_deletion_sites,
    "# Ins" = num_insertions,
    "# Ins Sites" = num_insertion_sites,
    "Genome Completeness" = genome_completeness,
    "QC Pass" = qc_pass
  )

if ("reference" %in% colnames(df)) {
  df <- df %>%
    rename("Segment Reference Name" = reference)
}

# Separate as its not an ONT output
if ("num_iupacs" %in% colnames(df)) {
  df <- df %>%
    rename(
      "# IUPACs" = num_iupacs
    )
}
# Lineage for covid
if ("lineage" %in% colnames(df)) {
  df <- df %>%
    rename(
      "Lineage" = lineage
    )
}

# Add color to table
df$completeness_int_color <- add_pass_value_int(df, 'QC Pass')

# Table#
table_number <- table_number + 1
table_label <- paste0("Table ", as.roman(table_number))

# Group segmented-virus rows by sample while retaining the segment reference.
table_options <- list(
  scrollX = FALSE,
  pageLength = 10,
  scrollY = "",
  columnDefs = list(
    list(className = 'dt-left', targets = "_all"),
    list(visible = FALSE, targets = 'completeness_int_color')
  )
)
if (isTRUE(params$segmented) && "reference" %in% colnames(summary_df)) {
  table_options$rowGroup <- list(dataSrc = 0)
  table_options$orderFixed <- list(pre = list(list(0, "asc")))
  table_options$order <- list(list(1, "asc"))
  table_options$columnDefs <- append(
    table_options$columnDefs,
    list(list(visible = FALSE, targets = 0))
  )
}

# Using datatable, removing the index row and adding in highlights for the status
summary_dt <- df %>%
  DT::datatable(
    rownames = FALSE,
    extensions = "RowGroup",
    caption = htmltools::tags$caption(
      style = 'caption-side: top',
      htmltools::strong(table_label), ' All Samples Data Summary'
    ),
    options = table_options
  ) %>%
  formatStyle('completeness_int_color',
    target = 'row',
    backgroundColor = styleEqual(c(1, 2, 3, 0),
    c('', 'orange', '#FFFF66', '#FF6666')
  )) %>%
  formatStyle('Genome Completeness',
    background = styleColorBar(range(0,1), 'lightblue', angle = -90),
    backgroundSize = '88% 88%',
    backgroundRepeat = 'no-repeat',
    backgroundPosition = 'left'
  )

summary_dt
```

## Row

### {-}
```{r median-depth-plot, error=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
# Getting all the depth TSV files
files <- list.files("base_coverages", pattern = "\\.bed$", full.names = TRUE)

# Combine all dfs
long_df <- rbindlist(
  lapply(files, fread,
    select = c("reference_name", "position", "depth"),
    colClasses = c(
      reference_name = "character",
      position = "integer",
      depth = "integer"
    )
  )
)

# Summarize positions
#  Ymin and Ymax for drawing the stdev region
#  Ymin should not be below 0
summary_depth_df <- long_df %>%
  group_by(reference_name, position) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(depth, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(depth, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(depth, na.rm = TRUE),
    ymin = pmax(mean - sd, 0),
    ymax = mean + sd,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

if (isTRUE(params$segmented)) {
  # Single plot with a dropdown to toggle between segments, resetting the
  # x-axis range to each segment's own genome length when switched.
  depth_segment_data <- split(summary_depth_df, summary_depth_df$reference_name)
  depth_segment_names <- names(depth_segment_data)
  p <- plot_ly()

  for (i in seq_along(depth_segment_data)) {
    segment_df <- depth_segment_data[[i]]
    p <- p %>%
      add_ribbons(
        data = segment_df,
        x = ~position,
        ymin = ~ymin,
        ymax = ~ymax,
        fillcolor = "rgba(0, 0, 255, 0.25)",
        line = list(color = "transparent"),
        name = "Mean ± SD",
        hoverinfo = "skip",
        visible = i == 1
      ) %>%
      add_lines(
        data = segment_df,
        x = ~position,
        y = ~median,
        line = list(color = "blue"),
        text = ~paste0(
          "<b>Position: </b>", position,
          "<br><b>Mean ± SD: </b>", round(mean, 2), " ± ", round(sd, 2)
        ),
        hoverinfo = "text",
        name = "Median read depth",
        visible = i == 1
      )
  }

  # Each segment contributes 2 traces (ribbon + line), so toggle both together.
  depth_segment_lengths <- vapply(
    depth_segment_data,
    function(segment_df) max(segment_df$position, na.rm = TRUE),
    numeric(1)
  )

  depth_segment_buttons <- lapply(seq_along(depth_segment_names), function(i) {
    visible <- rep(FALSE, length(depth_segment_names) * 2)
    visible[c(2 * i - 1, 2 * i)] <- TRUE

    list(
      label = depth_segment_names[[i]],
      method = "update",
      args = list(
        list(visible = visible),
        list(
          title = list(text = depth_segment_names[[i]], x = 0.5),
          xaxis = list(title = "Genome Position", range = c(0, depth_segment_lengths[[i]]), nticks = 10, showgrid = FALSE, gridcolor = "#dadce0", griddash = "dot", tickformat = ".0f")
        )
      )
    )
  })

  p %>%
    layout(
      title = list(text = depth_segment_names[[1]], x = 0.5),
      xaxis = list(title = "Genome Position", range = c(0, depth_segment_lengths[[1]]), nticks = 10, showgrid = FALSE, gridcolor = "#dadce0", griddash = "dot", tickformat = ".0f"),
      yaxis = list(title = "Median read depth", rangemode = "tozero", showgrid = FALSE),
      showlegend = FALSE,
      updatemenus = list(list(
        type = "dropdown",
        direction = "down",
        x = 0,
        xanchor = "left",
        y = 1.12,
        yanchor = "top",
        pad = list(r = 0, t = 0),
        buttons = depth_segment_buttons
      ))
    )
} else {
  # Create one plot per segment, preserving each segment's position range.
  segment_plots <- lapply(
    split(summary_depth_df, summary_depth_df$reference_name),
    function(segment_df) {
      segment_name <- unique(segment_df$reference_name)
      genome_length <- max(segment_df$position, na.rm = TRUE)

      plot_ly(segment_df, x = ~position, text = ~paste0(
        "<b>Position: </b>", position,
        "<br><b>Mean ± SD: </b>", round(mean, 2), " ± ", round(sd, 2)
      ), hoverinfo = "text") %>%
        add_ribbons(ymin = ~ymin, ymax = ~ymax, fillcolor = "rgba(0, 0, 255, 0.25)", line = list(color = "transparent"), name = "Mean ± SD", hoverinfo = "skip") %>%
        add_lines(y = ~median, line = list(color = "blue"), name = "Median read depth") %>%
        layout(title = list(text = segment_name, x = 0.5),
          xaxis = list(title = "Genome Position", range = c(0, genome_length), nticks = 10, showgrid = FALSE, gridcolor = "#dadce0", griddash = "dot", tickformat = ".0f"),
          yaxis = list(title = "Median read depth", rangemode = "tozero", showgrid = FALSE),
          showlegend = FALSE
        )
    }
  )

  subplot(
    segment_plots,
    nrows = length(segment_plots),
    shareX = FALSE,
    shareY = FALSE,
    titleX = TRUE,
    titleY = TRUE
  )
}
```


> **Figure 2.** Median summarized genomic read depth with standard deviation. The median depth and standard deviation were calculated for each genomic position and plotted such that the median depth is highlighted plus and minus 1 standard deviation.

```{r, software_ver, echo=FALSE, error=TRUE}
# Read the YAML file
yaml_data <- yaml::read_yaml("software_versions.yml")

# Track to build df
process <- c()
softwares <- c()
versions <- c()

# Loop over the data to build df
for (key_process in names(yaml_data)) {
  process_hash <- yaml_data[[key_process]]

  for (software_name in names(process_hash)) {
    software_version <- process_hash[[software_name]]

    # Add to lists
    process <- c(process, key_process)
    softwares <- c(softwares, software_name)
    versions <- c(versions, software_version)
  }
}

# Create table
table_number <- table_number + 1
table_label <- paste0("Table ", as.roman(table_number))

df <- data.frame("Process Name" = process, "Software" = softwares, "Version" = versions)
ddt <- df %>%
  DT::datatable(
    rownames = FALSE,
    class = 'cell-border stripe',
    caption = htmltools::tags$caption(
      style = 'caption-side: top',
      htmltools::strong(table_label), ' Software Versions'
    ),
    options = list(
      scrollX = FALSE,
      scrollY = "",
      columnDefs = list(
        list(className = 'dt-left', targets = "_all")
  )))
ddt
```
